- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 71.17 → 73.34 in Example 1).
- Model shows persistent lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast before model adjusts.
- Mean reversion is under-estimated — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price reverts to lower mean.
- Forecasts often overshoot in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, especially after a strong upward move.
- Model exhibits “overconfidence” in short-term momentum — fails to account for volatility decay or policy-induced corrections.
- When history includes a strong downward trend, model tends to underestimate the depth of the drop (e.g., 72.52 → 64.92 in Example 4).
- Forecasts are more sensitive to recent high prices than to long-term mean or seasonal patterns.
